title: Function-signature check diffs against an explicit base revision, not a fetched branch or merge-base
answers: function signature check fails in PR CI with missing base branch
signature check breaks on shallow checkout or limited git history
breaking-change check cannot find merge base in CI
how does the signature check choose what to compare against
body:
Symptom: the PR lint job's function-signature (breaking-change) check fails or cannot compare against the base branch, and the outcome depends on how much git history the checkout fetched.
Root cause: dev/check_function_signatures.py:get_changed_python_files fetched the base branch and ran three-dot `git diff base...HEAD` (merge-base discovery), and .github/workflows/lint.yml relied on fetch-depth 300 to hope the merge base was present locally.
Fix pattern: pass an explicit base revision and use two-dot `git diff --name-only BASE HEAD` plus `git show BASE:path` (dev/check_function_signatures.py:get_file_content_at_revision). PR CI passes `--base-revision HEAD^1` (first parent of the synthetic merge) with fetch-depth 2.
Constraints: HEAD^1 only exists on pull_request events, so the lint step must stay guarded by `github.event_name == 'pull_request'`. Reintroducing three-dot merge-base syntax or a deep fetch-depth brings back the history dependency.
applies: Applies to dev/check_function_signatures.py and the 'Check function signatures' step in .github/workflows/lint.yml; not to product code under mlflow/.
says: Pull request checks fail when comparing API function signatures against the target branch.
The automated pull request lint job cannot find the base branch to compare changes.
Ensure the breaking change checker can compare revisions on a shallow repository checkout.
Signature verification on pull requests breaks whenever the checkout commit history is limited.
